facts.value: Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia / small lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL/SLL) is a B-cell lymphoma comprising monomorphic small mature B cells that frequently coexpress CD5 and CD23.
9823/3 Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia / small lymphocytic lymphoma
2A82.0Z Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma
Follicular lymphoma (FL) is a neoplasm of germinal-centre (GC) B cells with varying proportions of centrocytes and centroblasts.
Essential: B-cell lymphoma composed of varying proportions of centrocytes and/or centroblasts; immunophenotype compatible.
Desirable: at least partly follicular growth pattern; BCL2 or BCL6 rearrangements.
Hairy cell leukaemia (HCL) is an indolent mature B-cell neoplasm composed of neoplastic cells with abundant cytoplasm and characteristic hairy projections.
characteristic morphology in a blood or marrow smear; immunophenotype CD11c, CD25, CD103.
clonal BRAF p.V600E mutation; positivity for CD123, CD200 (bright), cyclin D1.
Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma (LPL) is a neoplasm comprising small B lymphocytes, plasmacytoid lymphocytes, and plasma cells.
Essential: significant bone marrow infiltration by clonal small lymphocytes with plasmacytoid and/or plasma cell differentiation; IgM+.
Desirable: detection of MYD88 p.L265P; CXCR4 variant; monoclonal IgM.
Mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) is a mature B-cell neoplasm typically composed of small to medium-sized monomorphic cells expressing CD5, SOX11, and cyclin D1.
Cyclin D1–positive MCL Essential: lymphoma cells of B lineage (positive for CD20 and usually CD5); cyclin D1 positivity.
Cyclin D1–positive MCL Desirable: SOX11 expression positivity.
Splenic B-cell lymphoma/leukaemia with prominent nucleoli (SBLPN) is a splenic B-cell neoplasm with some but not all of the features of hairy cell leukaemia.
9591/3 Splenic B-cell lymphoma/leukaemia with prominent nucleoli
2A82.3 Splenic B-cell lymphoma or leukaemia, unclassifiable
Essential: circulating medium-sized lymphoid cells with prominent nucleoli or convoluted nuclei.
Desirable: diffuse involvement of the splenic red pulp; absence of BRAF mutation.
Splenic diffuse red pulp small B-cell lymphoma (SDRPL) is a small B-cell lymphoma involving the spleen, bone marrow, and peripheral blood.
9591/3 Splenic diffuse red pulp small B-cell lymphoma
2A82.Y Other specified mature B-cell neoplasm with leukaemic behaviour
diffuse infiltration of the spleen by monomorphic small B cells; peripheral blood with circulating small cells with villous projections.
absence of BRAF p.V600E mutation; absence of lymphadenopathy.
Splenic marginal zone lymphoma (SMZL) is an indolent mature B-cell neoplasm primarily presenting in the spleen, often with villous lymphocytes in the peripheral blood.
small B-cell lymphoma involving bone marrow and/or peripheral blood, composed of small lymphoid cells with villous processes; positive for IgM and IgD, negative for BCL6, ANXA1, CD103.
neoplastic cells that are negative for CD5 and CD10.

We need to produce integrated haematopathology report. Determine predicted_diagnosis.

Given evidence: immunophenotyping shows CD5+, CD19+, CD20+, CD23+, CD81 weak, CD200 positive, ROR1 negative, CD79b weak, CD43 positive, CD10 negative. Morphology: small_size positive, smear_cell positive, large_size negative, medium_size not mentioned, prolymphocyte not mentioned, prominent_nucleoli negative. So small mature B cells with CD5 and CD23 positivity typical of CLL/SLL. Also IGHV unmutated (p_54). del(11q) positive, del(17p) positive. t(11;14) negative. So fits CLL/SLL.

Also context: WBC 149.7, lymph 143.2 high, no paraprotein, splenomegaly absent but lymphadenopathy present. That could be SLL (nodal). But immunophenotype and cytogenetics support CLL/SLL. The presence of del(17p) indicates poor prognosis.

Thus predicted_diagnosis: CLL/SLL.

key_findings.description: Small mature B‑cell morphology (small size, smear cell positive)

differential.rationale: The patient shows the classic immunophenotype (CD5+, CD23+) and small mature B‑cell morphology, with cytogenetic abnormalities (del11q, del17p) and high lymphocytosis typical of CLL/SLL.
Absence of germinal‑center markers (CD10 negative) and lack of follicular morphology make FL unlikely.
BRAF mutation is absent and villous projections were not described, arguing against HCL.
No IgM paraprotein and no plasmacytoid morphology exclude LPL/WM.
CD23 positivity and lack of cyclin D1 data make MCL unlikely.
The cells are small and lack prominent nucleoli, inconsistent with SBLPN.
Absence of splenomegaly and lack of villous projections argue against SDRPL.
The patient is CD5 positive and IgM negative, which excludes SMZL.

discriminators.text: CD5+ and CD23+ immunophenotype with small mature B‑cell morphology
Presence of del(11q) and del(17p) cytogenetic abnormalities

unresolved: Absolute B‑cell count not provided to confirm CLL versus SLL
would_change: If CD23 were negative or if the cells expressed CD10 and BCL6, FL would become more likely.
Detection of a BRAF V600E mutation or villous projections would support HCL.
Identification of IgM monoclonal protein or plasmacytoid differentiation would favor LPL/WM.
